Alyssa (CS): Heads-up — Greenlane's exec sponsor asked for a short SLA/SLO writeup for the onboarding review tomorrow. They want uptime, latency targets, and how credits would be calculated if we miss.
Miguel (AM): Agree, we should include: p50/p95 latency for their baseline workload, maintenance windows, and a simple credit formula. Also note renewal risk if missed SLOs repeat across two months.
Sophia (Onboarding): I can pull the onboarding perf runs and a 7-day tail latency heatmap. Question: do we promise p95 <= 220ms or 300ms for the first 30 days? Greenlane's traffic is bursty.
Jordan (SE): For initial ramp I'd recommend p95 <= 300ms, p50 <= 90ms. We can offer a 30-day ramp SLA where we target 300ms then tighten. Also call out KV/cache warmup impact on first 5k requests.
Alyssa (CS): Good. Can you draft a one-pager with both targets and the ramp policy + what triggers credits? I want it customer-ready by 11am PT.
Jordan (SE): Drafting now. Proposed credit calc snippet to include, simple and transparent:
```
credit = min( max(0, (SLO_target_seconds - observed_seconds) / SLO_target_seconds), 1.0 ) * monthly_commit_amount
```
Explain in words: prorated dollar credit up to 100% of monthly committed invoice for sustained breach windows.
Miguel (AM): Call out exceptions — scheduled maintenance (>=48h advance), customer misconfig, and DDoS events. Also include "two-strike" renewal clause: if 2 separate SLO breach months in a rolling 6-month window, CS + AM will escalate renewal terms.
Sophia (Onboarding): I'll attach the onboarding test artifacts and the CSV of tail latencies. Also propose a customer enablement session to walk their SREs through our tracing dashboard and suggested alerts. When should that be scheduled?
Alyssa (CS): Schedule after draft is approved. If Jordan finishes the draft in the next hour I'll review and we can offer a slot next Wed.
SLA-bot: [automated check] Greenlane env: recent daily uptime: 99.98%, 7d p95 latency: 278ms, p50: 105ms. No incidents in last 14 days.
Jordan (SE): Updated doc attached in thread (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/drafts/1999000001). Key callouts:
- Ramp policy: Month 0-1 p95 <= 300ms, Month 2+ p95 <= 220ms
- Credit policy: monthly-prorated for sustained 1+ hour windows where p95 > target by >20%
- Measurement: server-side p95 over 5-minute rolling windows, exclude planned maintenance and customer-generated load spikes (per runbook)
- Feedback loop: we capture post-onboarding NPS + a 6-week technical health survey to catch perf regressions early
Miguel (AM): Looks good. Add a short blurb about how credits are applied on the next invoice and that credits do not alter contractual commitments unless repeated breaches occur.
Alyssa (CS): I'll fold Miguel's blurb and send to Greenlane with a short enablement invite. Action items: 1) Jordan finalize doc with runbook snippet (due in 45m), 2) Sophia export latency CSV + set up dashboard demo (due EOD), 3) Miguel prepare renewal-risk paragraph for the one-pager, 4) Alyssa send to customer after review.
Sophia (Onboarding): On it — starting dashboard demo prep now.
Jordan (SE): Draft updated, added runbook excerpt for measurement and sample alerting thresholds. Pushed to the draft link.
Alyssa (CS): Thx team. If anything looks risky re: credits/regression language ping me immediately.
Miguel (AM): Will do. /cc @Greenlane-eng when we send. :thumbsup:
SLA-bot: [note] Saved snapshot of metrics used for SLO calc: bucket=greenlane, snapshot_ts=1999000002.
